summary: LUNAR QUEST is a browser-based 3D lunar mission simulation designed for children aged 7–12. Players become astronaut commanders, explore a lunar outpost and solve interactive survival challenges involving oxygen, water, electricity, food production, radiation protection and communication delays. Through visual storytelling and consequence-driven decisions, children experience how limited resources create real engineering trade-offs in space exploration. The project incorporates NASA space-weather information and educational resources, clearly distinguishing authentic scientific data from simulated gameplay. LUNAR QUEST transforms complex space-engineering concepts into an engaging, accessible learning adventure.
details:
Project Overview

LUNAR QUEST is an interactive 3D lunar outpost simulation that transforms space survival engineering into an engaging learning experience for children aged 7–12.

Players take the role of an astronaut commander and explore a virtual lunar base containing essential facilities such as the astronaut habitat, power station, greenhouse, radiation shelter, communication station and rover station.

Existing Approach vs. Proposed Solution

Existing Approach

  • Space concepts are often taught through textbooks, videos and static learning materials.
  • Engineering trade-offs are explained theoretically.
  • Children have limited opportunities to experiment with resource management.
  • Space-survival systems are often learned as separate topics.
  • Learning may focus more on remembering facts than applying knowledge.

Proposed Solution – LUNAR QUEST

  • An interactive 3D lunar outpost where children explore as astronaut commanders.
  • Realistic engineering trade-offs are experienced through mission-based decisions.
  • Children experiment with oxygen, water, electricity and food management.
  • Connected survival systems demonstrate how one decision affects the entire lunar base.
  • Visual storytelling and consequence-based gameplay encourage critical thinking and problem-solving.

How It Works

The experience follows a mission-based learning approach. Children discover problems, understand the situation through visual storytelling, make decisions and observe the consequences in the simulated lunar environment.

The gameplay introduces five important space-survival challenges:

  1. Life Support – Managing oxygen and water for astronaut survival.
  2. Power Management – Allocating limited electricity across essential systems.
  3. Radiation Protection – Understanding space-weather hazards and astronaut sheltering.
  4. Food Production – Balancing greenhouse lighting, water and plant growth.
  5. Communication Delay – Understanding why astronauts cannot always receive immediate responses from Earth.

Every decision involves resource trade-offs. For example, protecting solar panels from a simulated lunar dust hazard can reduce immediate electricity generation, forcing the commander to depend on stored battery power.

NASA Data and Scientific Foundation

The project uses NASA space-weather information from DONKI to introduce real solar energetic particle events and radiation-related learning scenarios. NASA lunar exploration resources, including Artemis and Earth's Moon educational information, provide scientific context.

Real NASA observations and educational information are distinguished from simulated resource values and fictional mission scenarios.

Technology

  • React, Vite and TypeScript – Web application development.
  • Three.js / React Three Fiber – Interactive 3D lunar environment.
  • Tailwind CSS – User interface styling.
  • Zustand – Game state management.
  • NASA open resources – Scientific information and educational context.
  • Browser LocalStorage – Local mission progress.

Innovation and Impact

Unlike conventional space-learning applications that primarily present facts or quizzes, LUNAR QUEST allows children to experience the consequences of engineering decisions.

Its combination of 3D exploration, mission-based storytelling, resource management and visual scientific explanations encourages critical thinking, problem-solving and an understanding of the real constraints involved in human space exploration.

The application is designed as an accessible browser-based experience without mandatory registration or installation.

Use of Artificial Intelligence

ChatGPT was used for project ideation, challenge analysis, educational content development and technical planning. Claude Code was used as an AI-assisted development tool for code generation, implementation, debugging and testing. The project architecture, integration decisions, gameplay requirements and final implementation were reviewed and directed by the development team.
